reader.requirement: At 1985 an item whose PICTURE is numeric (signed or not, scaled or not, usage DISPLAY) and that carries BLANK WHEN ZERO has category numeric edited for every rule keyed on category: it edits as a receiver (spaces when zero, no sign), de-edits as a sender to numeric, moves to alphanumeric without the noninteger bar, is no arithmetic operand or resultant (only a GIVING receiver), takes only a nonnumeric VALUE literal, is no UNSTRING receiver, compares as a nonnumeric operand, admits the ALPHABETIC test, and is NUMERIC-EDITED to INITIALIZE.

edition-consulted.switches: edition.DialectLevel < 2002 promotes a SIGNED numeric picture with BLANK WHEN ZERO to numeric edited (S dropped from the mask); from 2002 S beside the clause is refused (COBOL1934, §2023:13.18.40.3 SR22)
ConstructRegistry value-numeric-literal-numeric-edited-2023: a numeric VALUE literal on a numeric edited item is refused below 2023 (COBOL0900)

reader.edition-search: grep -i blank.?when.?zero over src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler; the promotion lives in PictureAnalyzer.AnalyzeCharacterString line 480, the only edition comparison on the path besides the VALUE construct gate.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: 1985 promotes PIC S9(n) BLANK WHEN ZERO (later editions refuse S beside the clause) and refuses a numeric VALUE literal on the promoted item (2023 admits it)
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witnesses cover editing on a zero store and the character comparison; the signed 1985-only form, de-editing, the alphanumeric and alphabetic receivers, arithmetic, VALUE, UNSTRING, STRING, the class test and INITIALIZE categories are not exercised

reader.notes: PictureAnalyzer returns a PicInfo of category NumericEdited for the clause's subject, so every consumer reads the category from one place; the 1985 arm also promotes a signed picture (kb/Work PB5191 per the code comment). Every probed consequence matched the 1985 text.

refuter.evidence: Read §1985:VI.5.4 whole and attacked category-keyed rules the reader did not try, at --std 85. bzA2: B PIC 9V99 BWZ holding '123': IF B = 123 -> T, IF B = NI (999) -> T, IF B = "123" -> T (character comparison, §1985:VI.6.3.1.1.2); BZ blank: IF BZ = ZERO -> F, = SPACES -> T; MOVE BZ (spaces) TO 9V99 -> [0.00] (de-edited); MOVE B TO ZZ9.99 -> [  1.23] (numeric edited to numeric edited de-edits, VI.6.19.4 GR4b); B NUMERIC -> true. bzB refusals: IF B = 1.23 and IF B = N (9V99) -> COBOL2532 (noninteger numeric vs nonnumeric, §1985:VI.6.3.1.1.2 rule 3); TE(BI) with BI 9 BWZ -> COBOL0844 (no numeric subscript); PERFORM VARYING BI -> COBOL2120; SET I UP BY BI -> COBOL2112. bzA: PIC S9(3) SIGN LEADING SEPARATE BLANK WHEN ZERO -> COBOL2422, consistent with GR2 because §1985:VI.5.12.3 SR1 admits SIGN only on a numeric entry and the item is numeric edited. Each consequence matches category numeric edited. A reading, noted but outside GR2: the 1985-only signed form drops the S (MOVE -12 stores 0012); 1985 lists no S among numeric edited symbols and its SIGN rules govern only numeric entries, so no rule of this edition keeps an operational sign there. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:VI.5.4.4 GR2  the text is in GR2'; 'OK  §1985:VI.6.3.1.1.2  it lies in SR3'; 'OK  §1985:VI.5.12.3 SR1  the text is in SR1'; 'OK  §1985:VI.6.19.4 GR4b  the text is in GR4b'.
